In Their Own Time

Feature documentary60–70 min Transylvania, RomaniaShooting 2026
The film

Every nation has a region it laughs at for being slow.

Romania's is Transylvania. This documentary takes the joke seriously — and finds that the slowness never existed. What existed was measure: a three-hundred-year-old habit of doing things properly, mistaken by everyone else for laziness.

A film about a stereotype that becomes a film about the price of speed, in a world exhausted by its own acceleration.

How it looks

Four Materials

The register is the contemporary video-essay at feature scale, with cinema craft — and a painted layer for everything the camera cannot reach. Oil, not diagram: the past is rendered the way the period rendered itself.

01
Studio

Three recurring voices in a controlled, stylised space. Built light, shot as a set — the film's spine.

02
Location

Cluj at rush hour, glass towers over baroque façades. A village clock still wound by hand. Archive rooms. Observational, patient, real light.

03
Archive

Period photography and film from the Transylvanian Museum of Ethnography.

04
Oil painting & data

Habsburg Vienna, the guilds, the scholar at his petition — painted in oil, visible brushwork, warm earth pigments, the palette of the archive itself. Plus map and data animation.

Production

A Real Crew

CrewA twenty-person film unit. Our own team, not a two-man documentary kit.
ShootSeven principal shooting days, plus an extended documentation period across the territory.
SetupsA built studio for the three voices, and location work across Cluj and greater Transylvania.
PostA long post: the animation build, generated historical imagery, original score, sound, colour, and an English international master.
TerritoryCluj County and greater Transylvania.

The camera package is not locked yet.

That is exactly why this conversation is happening now, and not after the shoot. Whatever goes on the truck in 2026 is what appears in every frame — and in the lesson we make about it.

What partners receive

A lesson, not a logo.

01
The how-it's-made

A full making-of built around the shoot — how the studio was lit, how the location work was handled, how the picture was built. In English. Your equipment in the hands of a working crew, explained by the people using it. This is the content your marketing team tries to produce every week and cannot make credible.

02
Yours to republish

The making-of and the set stills come to you with the right to use them in full, on your own channels, unedited or re-cut. We are not lending you a mention. We are handing you finished content.

03
Raw material

Behind-the-scenes footage and photography from every shooting day, delivered as usable files, not as a highlight reel we picked for you.

04
Credit

Your name in the film's end titles, on official materials, and in the communication around every screening. The politeness, after the substance.

Where it goes

Two Audiences

The film — Romania
  • Romanian streaming platforms
  • Our own channel
  • Cultural broadcast channels
  • Free across the Romanian cultural circuit — schools, libraries, cultural centres

A public-funded film with a public obligation: it stays free where it matters. That is what gives it institutional standing, and it is why the Council's name is on it.

The lesson — worldwide
  • In English, on YouTube, no territory
  • Aimed at filmmakers, students and film schools
  • Educational material has a long tail — it is watched for years, not for a week
  • Free for you to republish on your own channels

The film is Romanian. The lesson is not. Your customers are not in the Romanian cultural circuit — they are the people who search for how a documentary like this was lit and shot. That is the audience we hand you.
